NFLX: Fell 5.4% on Sep 4 in the tech sell-off and 7% the week of Sep 18 as Wells Fargo flagged engagement risk from YouTube; HSBC downgraded it on Sep 22.
BAC: Sep 14: fell about 5% (its worst day since April 2025) after CEO Brian Moynihan guided Q3 trading revenue roughly flat and flagged weaker investment-banking fees, dragging big banks. The Fed hiked on Sep 16, and Sep 22's Muse-driven AI fears hit banks again.
RTX: Slid 5% the week of Sep 4 and kept drifting; defense names slipped again Sep 22 on a report the Strait of Hormuz is reopening and US–Iran diplomacy progress. Its record $289B backlog is unchanged.
GS: Big-bank sell-off after BofA's Sep 14 warning on flat trading and weaker IB fees; fell 8.5% the week ending Sep 18 around the Fed's Sep 16 rate hike.
HD: Home Depot's CFO warned the U.S. housing market is "frozen" with turnover at historic lows; rising rates (Fed hike Sep 16) weigh on big-ticket DIY. Six straight down weeks before this week's bounce; near a 52-week low.
MS: Fell with big banks after BofA's Sep 14 trading/IB outlook; −2.9% Sep 22 as Muse and AI-advisor fears hit wealth managers.
MA: Payments names slipped with financials on Sep 22 AI-agent fears and stablecoin competition headlines (SoFi settling card payments on stablecoin). Only 7% off its August high.
GE: Aerospace pullback: fell 3.3% on Sep 15; commentary around a lower 2026 departures forecast. Six straight down weeks before bouncing 1.6% this week.
COST: Slow drift lower into fiscal Q4 earnings (Sep 24) at ~40× forward earnings; no single catalyst.
V: Slipped with financials on Sep 22 AI-agent fears; merchants challenging the card-fee settlement. Only ~6% off its August high.
JPM: Sep 22: fell ~3.4% as Meta's Muse agent (moves savings to higher-yield accounts automatically) and a Vanguard-backed AI advisor hit banks; also fell with peers after BofA's Sep 14 outlook.
UNH: Medicare Advantage margin concerns linger ahead of Oct 13 earnings; fell 4.6% the week of Sep 11 around its ex-dividend date.
WFC: Fell 3.9% Sep 22 as Muse added to AI-disruption fears in banks; also hit by BofA's Sep 14 outlook and the Fed hike.
CSCO: Sep 22: fell 4.5% after Piper Sandler cut its price target on growth concerns, while the rest of tech rose.
PANW: Fell 9.3% on Sep 2 in the early-September software sell-off but has since bounced ~10%; roughly flat for the month.
AMZN: Small pullback; in the news for blocking rival AI shopping agents (e.g. Muse) on its site. Down ~10% from its Aug 3 high.
MSFT: Modest giveback after a big summer run (+33% over 3 months); no specific catalyst.
CVX: Oil pulled back from above $100 on US–Iran diplomacy and a Hormuz reopening report; Goldman trimmed its target to $228. Fell from a Sep 15 record high.
AVGO: Chip volatility (fell 4.8% Sep 14 when AI leaders urged a development slowdown); bouncing +1.9% this week.
XOM: Oil fell mid-month on diplomacy optimism; down ~6% from a Sep 15 peak.
PLTR: Essentially flat after a 40% August surge; bouncing this week.
KO: Essentially unchanged (−0.1%); Teamsters strike at some Coca-Cola facilities in the news.
CHTR: Broadband subscriber bleed (≈292K internet subs lost in H1) to T-Mobile fixed wireless, fiber and Starlink. Fell 8% on Sep 9 after Comcast's CFO called broadband pricing "irrational"; Wolfe downgrade and Cox-merger debt worries added on. At a new 52-week low.
CASY: Fiscal Q1 (Sep 8) beat on profit, but inside same-store sales slowed to 3.2% (from 4%+) and the market doubts fuel-margin gains will last. Guidance left unchanged. Dropped 14% on Sep 9, worst in the S&P that day.
COO: Q3 miss and a Q4 EPS guide of $1.05–1.09 vs. $1.19 expected; scrapped the CooperSurgical sale that bulls were counting on; U.S. contact-lens channel destocking. Fell 15% on Sep 10. An activist is now pushing for a CEO change.
FICO: Sep 4: FHFA said Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will accept the far cheaper VantageScore in place of FICO, threatening FICO's mortgage-score pricing power. Fell 17% that day; new 52-week low today.
AXON: Sold off 10% on Sep 15 after announcing a ~$1B zero-coupon convertible note offering, on top of worries about Q2 gross-margin slippage (62.9%, down 40 bp) from memory costs.
ADBE: Sep 4: surprise internal CEO succession announced ahead of earnings plus a soft Q4 outlook; fell 7% and reignited AI-disruption fears across creative and enterprise software.
INTU: Investor day in late August reset the growth outlook lower; caught in repeated software sell-offs on AI-disruption fears (e.g. Sep 19 with CrowdStrike, HubSpot, Okta).
BKNG: Fell 6.7% Sep 8 on EU Digital Markets Act search-visibility worries and competition, then a blocked eTraveli deal; Sep 22 Meta's Muse AI agent triggered a travel-booking sell-off. Six straight down weeks.
DASH: Slid with consumer-internet names in early September on delivery-competition and profitability worries (−5.3% Sep 8). No single company catalyst found; the $131M NYC pay settlement on Sep 22 was taken in stride.
CMCSA: Sep 9: fell 6.6% after the CFO described broadband pricing as "irrational" — read as a price war with fixed-wireless and fiber rivals while broadband subs keep shrinking.
EFX: Fell 6.4% on Sep 4 alongside FICO after the FHFA credit-score decision, adding uncertainty to mortgage credit-reporting economics.
ADSK: Dropped 8.3% on Sep 4 in the software sell-off triggered by Adobe's CEO news, already under pressure after late-August guidance disappointed.
SYK: Sep 8: fell 8.8% after the CFO said supply disruptions in the peripheral-vascular business will continue into Q4 instead of clearing by the end of Q3.
ROP: Vertical-software exposure caught in the broad AI-disruption de-rating; a steady six-day losing streak with no single catalyst found.
FIS: Bank-tech and payments names keep de-rating; Piper Sandler initiated at Neutral ($42) on Sep 11; the Sep 22 "consumer inertia" sell-off hit financials. Trading at a 52-week low.
CMG: Fell 5.9% on Sep 15 on a salmonella headline and profit-taking; weak August restaurant traffic and a Baird downgrade weigh on the group.
GIS: Cost inflation and soft volumes heading into fiscal Q1 earnings (Sep 23); sentiment on packaged food remains poor.
OMC: Lost the PepsiCo media account (reported Sep 2–3), falling ~5%; ongoing worry that AI erodes agency economics.
LULU: Sep 4: plunged 17% after a second straight full-year guidance cut and weak Q2 sales as a new CEO starts. Hit an 8-year low mid-month.
FISV: Continued de-rating after its 2025 collapse; printed another 52-week low on Sep 22, the same day its former CFO was named CFO of Pentair. Seven straight down days.
BRO: Softening property-insurance pricing is squeezing broker organic growth; the group also took read-through hits from Aon's USI deal and the Sep 22 Muse AI-agent sell-off.
ALB: China lithium prices sliding again and EV-demand doubts; Mizuho cut its target to $140 on Sep 18. Bounced 5% this week.
BX: Alt-manager sell-off continues on private-credit stress, redemption caps and fund-exit worries; fell 4.6% on Sep 1. Five straight down weeks.
SLB: Pulled back from an Aug 31 record as oil eased mid-month on US–Iran diplomacy and a report that the Strait of Hormuz is reopening; profit-taking after a 54% one-year run.
DPZ: Baird downgraded Domino's (and Chipotle) as restaurant traffic weakened; fell 4.2% on Sep 9.
ARES: Same private-credit and alt-manager de-rating hitting Blackstone and KKR.
CPRT: Fiscal Q4 (Sep 10) EPS of $0.35 missed the $0.38 estimate, it launched a $1.9B tender for ACV Auctions, and HSBC downgraded it.
RCL: High oil and fuel costs pressure cruise margins; fell 6% today (Sep 22) on reports it is near a deal for a majority stake in Sandals Resorts. Six straight down weeks, at a 52-week low.
AJG: Broker group weakness on softening pricing, Aon/USI read-through and the Sep 22 Muse sell-off.
LDOS: Government-services names drifting lower; no single September catalyst found. Five straight down weeks.
GEN: Fell 6.4% today (Sep 22) with consumer-subscription names in the Muse sell-off; no company-specific news found. Only 6 trading days off its high.
NCLH: Oil at elevated levels undercuts fuel-cost relief hopes; Norwegian and Carnival hit 52-week lows in September. Six straight down weeks.
FDS: Fell 5.8% on Sep 10 amid worries about AI reshaping financial-data workflows; peaked Aug 31, so this is a fresh pullback, not a long slide.
ABNB: Travel booking sold off as Meta's Muse agent (can book trips directly) went viral Sep 22; also slipped with Booking/Expedia on Sep 8. Only 19 days off its high.
EXPE: Fell 7.9% Sep 8 with Booking; hit again Sep 22 as Muse raised fears of AI agents disintermediating online travel agencies.
EXE: Natural-gas producers weak; fell 5.8% Sep 16. No company-specific catalyst found.
ODFL: Record ~$6 diesel is squeezing freight margins (J.B. Hunt had its worst day since 2020) and Amazon's LTL expansion looms. Six straight down weeks until this week's bounce.
VRSK: Barclays cut its target $275→$225 on Sep 8; worry that AI commoditizes insurance data, amplified by the Muse sell-off in insurers.
JKHY: Bank-tech peer weakness; fell 6.4% Sep 15. No single company catalyst found.
CBOE: Trading-volume and volatility normalization after the spring spike; down ~27% from its May high.
TYL: Government-software de-rating on AI fears; CEO stock sale and Axon's convert weighed on the group.
AON: Announced a $17B purchase of USI Insurance Services from KKR on Aug 31 and fell ~10% that day on price and leverage worries; kept sliding in September (six straight down days) as analysts cut targets. At a 52-week low.
FDXF: Diesel squeeze on LTL carriers plus a leadership shake-up (commercial chief out, Sep 14); Goldman cut its target to $171.
ALL: Sep 22: fell 5.5% as Meta's Muse AI agent — which can shop for and switch insurance policies automatically — sparked a sell-off in insurers.
CVNA: High-beta name drifting lower with consumer-credit and used-car worries; no single catalyst found.
WTW: Broker group weakness on softening pricing, Aon/USI read-through and the Muse sell-off.
HAL: Oil weakness in mid-September on US–Iran diplomacy optimism, ahead of Q3 earnings on Oct 20.
CLX: Doubts about margin recovery; Barclays target cut; hit a 52-week low Sep 18 before a bounce this week.
BR: Concern that AI and tokenized equities threaten its proxy and investor-communications franchise.

_stories.sub: Three forces explain most of this list.

tiles.p: Adobe's surprise CEO change and soft outlook on Sep 4 reignited worries that AI undercuts software pricing. Autodesk, Intuit, Roper, Tyler and data providers followed.
tiles.t: ADBE · INTU · ADSK · ROP · VRSK · BR · FDS · TYL

tiles.p: Meta's Muse AI agent, which shops, books trips and switches insurance and savings on its own, hit No. 1 on the App Store and sparked selling in travel, insurers and banks.
tiles.t: BKNG · EXPE · ABNB · ALL · JPM · WFC

tiles.p: Oil near $100 and record diesel hit cruise lines and truckers, while energy stocks pulled back as US–Iran diplomacy advanced. The Fed raised rates to 3.75–4.00% on Sep 16.
tiles.t: RCL · NCLH · ODFL · FDXF · SLB · HAL
